title: Record a c=1 stabilizer transporter of one 8-dimensional joint basis
body:
<!-- CURSOR_AGENT_PR_BODY_BEGIN -->

## Change and mathematical scope

Finite exact certificate. No new κ, and the selected frontier is unchanged at `781451/250000000`.

For the historical 8-by-112 centre query, the unsigned involution `sigma = (0 3)(5 6)` lies in the order-3072 stabilizer of sector `c=1` and outside the group generated by `H`, `g` and `t`. It carries the pinned 8-dimensional `(+1,+1)` basis from PR #7019 onto the `(+1,-1)` joint space: each canonical basis vector is sent to the canonical basis vector with the same address coefficients on coordinate 3.

The same run is an exhaustive census of that stabilizer. Every element carries the basis onto exactly one of the four joint spaces, 768 elements each. The three spaces other than `(+1,+1)` account for 2304 elements, all outside `<H, g, t>`. Another 704 elements outside that group preserve the `(+1,+1)` space; the order-64 group itself is contained in the 768-element stabilizer of that space.

In the ordered bases, `B = 4 A_1` has the same 8-by-8 matrix on the `(+1,+1)` and `(+1,-1)` spaces, so the witness intertwines those two restrictions. The degree-8 polynomial is not recomputed. The degree-216 polynomial and the 216-by-216 nullity are not touched. This is not the 8-dimensional dihedral isotypic summand inside the trivial-character 216-space.

Evidence class: one finite identity, plus an exhaustive census of a set of order 3072. The symmetry group is the signed affine group of order 344064, the orbit of address `1` has size 112, and the `T(1) = 1` scan matches that count. This is not a heuristic search and not an unrestricted claim about operators outside the stabilizer.

## Task and overlap

- Task: `formal-interface-lemma`, scope changed.
- Upstream base: `17469fff78c22941280f04d39dc5a1faee09c840` (priority revision 8).
- Open question from PR #7019: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7019
- Package: `research/c1-joint-8-transporter/`
- Fork head: https://github.com/unpaidmoon/integer-mult-bounds/tree/cursor/c1-joint-8-transporter-3fe3 at `eda1117b3989bc24ea0f8331cbac774f4bfe0593`

The catalogue card asks for a formal caller binding. The live remainder is the transporter left open by PR #7019. The trace formula and the characteristic polynomial do not exhibit an element outside `<H, g, t>`.

Overlap on 2026-11-10 against upstream `17469fff78c22941280f04d39dc5a1faee09c840`: local notes 10178 of 10178 HEAD paths, complete; 339 open PRs, pagination complete, fetched 2026-11-10T10:34:04Z. The discussion refresh hit a GitHub rate limit, so discussion coverage is not claimed. The phrases `8-dimensional joint` and `outside the group generated` matched PR #7019, which asks this question, and matched PR #7023 only where it says it does not treat these joint spaces. No open-PR body exhibits this transporter.

Open PR #7022 censuses the trivial-character 216-space. Open PR #7023 splits a different 8-dimensional summand. Neither carries this basis.

Selected-baseline orientation returned `PASS_RESEARCH_BASELINE_BINDINGS_ONLY` for kappa `781451/250000000`.

## Validation

CPython 3.12.3, standard library only. Marker: `PASS_C1_JOINT_8_TRANSPORTER`.

```sh
python3 -B -W error research/c1-joint-8-transporter/verify.py
python3 -B -O research/c1-joint-8-transporter/verify.py
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/c1-joint-8-transporter --check-only
```

`scripts/research_package.py --package research/c1-joint-8-transporter` returned `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`. Acceptance uses explicit checks, so `-O` does not skip a census step or a rejection control. On the measured host the census takes about five seconds.

The verifier rebuilds `AGL(3,2)`, the order-3072 stabilizer, the group `<H, g, t>` of order 64, and the inherited basis. It checks the witness vector by vector, checks that the pattern test and the eigenvalue test agree on all 3072 elements, and checks that both restrictions of `B` equal the pinned 8-by-8 matrix. Rejection controls cover a coordinate transposition, the bare transposition `(0 3)`, a lone minus sign on coordinate 0, a flipped basis coefficient, a deleted pattern, and a `(+1,+1)` vector tested against the `(+1,-1)` equations.

Not run: Lean, Docker, the degree-881 replay, the degree-216 replay, and the selected cold replay.

## Credit

Prepared by unpaidmoon with substantial Cursor Grok assistance.

PR #7019 recorded the character, the basis pivots and the common matrix, and left this transporter unconstructed. PR #6944 supplied `H`, `g`, `t` and the dimension 8. The sector-3 census in `research/c3-centre-sign-split/` is the model for the signed affine enumeration; the sector here is `c=1`. JoyboyBrian's handoff recorded the original decomposition question. Ali Romman's PR4958 and PR4720 retain the query and the Bell action. Krzysztof Wojt's exact one-slot package is the degree-881 annihilator, not replayed here. Nick Petalas's PR5120 is the degree-410 lower bound. The doubled representation comes from PR1719. New work is Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

- What is the image in `GL(V)` of the 768-element setwise stabilizer of this `(+1,+1)` joint space? 704 of those elements lie outside `<H, g, t>` and still preserve `V`. A scalar image would mean they do not split `V` any further. This `V` is the `chi` joint space, not the 8-dimensional dihedral isotypic summand of the trivial-character 216-space. First step: restrict to the ordered basis one diagonal element that is minus on all of `L = {0,3,4,7}` and plus on the complement, and compare the matrix with `±I`.
